strengths: Well-motivated clinical design grounded in radiologist workflow (coarse-to-fine scanning, regional analysis, quantitative assessment) with effective illustration in Figure 1

Practical system design addressing real clinical needs: explicit quantitative attribute extraction, structured report format alignment with clinical workflows, deterministic and interpretable attribute computation

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: SlowFast strategy is adapted unchanged from video recognition [11]; mask pooling and region-aware extraction are incremental over Osprey [48], MAIRA-SEG [37], and Reg2RG [7]; lesion attribute extraction is deterministic rule-based processing. Critical brittleness from external segmentation dependency: entire framework relies on TotalSegmentator; Supplementary Tab. S5 shows 31% BLEU drop with organ mask distortion; small lesion detection bounded by 69% miss rate of upstream segmentor (110/160 cases with ≤5mm³ nodules); no mitigation strategy proposed

Evaluation methodology concerns: (1) Ground-truth reports restructured using LLM (Llama-3.3-70B) creating potential circularity in downstream evaluation; (2) Radiologist reader study limited to one resident on 50 cases without inter-rater reliability; (3) Clinical accuracy evaluation depends on proprietary GPT-5-nano API (not reproducible); (4) Custom 6-region structured format may bias results in favor of the proposed approach

Narrow domain specialization with poor generalization: entire approach is chest CT-specific with fixed anatomical taxonomy tied to TotalSegmentator; external dataset only 500 cases; zero-shot generalization shows 65% relative decline (GREEN: 0.4555→0.1572); no evidence of transferability to other modalities or anatomies

Insufficient architectural justification: design choices lack ablation or motivation (e.g., kernel=2 in slow pathway, specific layer indices 6/12/18/24 for mask pooling, input resolution 448×448×128, six-organ taxonomy selection); some hyperparameters appear arbitrary; incomplete comparison (Reg2RG [7] mentioned but not compared)

Limited clinical validation: single radiologist assessment insufficient for deployment claims; no sensitivity/specificity analysis; no comparison of inter-radiologist agreement vs model performance; reader study results (6.98/10 vs 4.44 for next best) lack clinical threshold definition for adequacy

Incomplete failure analysis: large airway underperformance (Supplementary Tab. S1) not thoroughly analyzed; small nodule failures attributed to segmentation with no proposed solutions; no systematic error taxonomy beyond size stratification

Reproducibility gaps despite supplementary materials: code unavailable at review; two-stage training procedure complexity not fully specified; mask interpolation to feature resolution not detailed; statistical significance tests between methods absent despite confidence intervals; bootstrap analysis without hypothesis testing

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: SlowFast strategy borrowed from video recognition [11], Mask-Driven Visual Extractor adapted from Osprey [48], pseudo-mask generation uses off-the-shelf TotalSegmentator [43], and lesion attribute extraction is straightforward mask-based computation. Critical dependency on segmentation quality creates fundamental performance bottleneck: organ mask distortion causes 31% BLEU drop (Table S5); small lesion detection (≤5mm³) achieves only 0.127 vs. baselines 0.3-0.4 due to upstream segmentation failures; model performance inherently capped by segmentation quality

Concerning generalization gaps contradicting 'robust generalization' claims: GREEN score drops 65% on external data (0.4555→0.1572), BLEU drops 63% (0.3435→0.1275); external dataset modest at 500 test cases; zero-shot transfer shows practical failure

Narrow architectural scope: framework is tightly coupled to TotalSegmentator's 6-region label space; claim of 'model-agnostic architecture' is misleading; generalization to other anatomies, modalities, or tasks is undiscussed; only single-task evaluation on structured reporting

Lack of systematic failure analysis: only one successful case in main paper and one in ablations; no error pattern analysis; unclear when region masking helps vs. hurts; handling of anatomical variants or lesions crossing region boundaries not addressed

Limited novelty for ECCV: primarily applies existing vision techniques (SlowFast, masking) to medical application; NLP contributions (structured reporting, attribute extraction) outside ECCV scope; better suited for medical imaging or clinical applications venues
